name: Andrej Plenković
role: Prime Minister of the Republic of Croatia (predsjednik Vlade Republike Hrvatske)
party: Hrvatska demokratska zajednica (HDZ) — European People's Party (EPP)
bio: Andrej Plenković, born in Zagreb in 1970, is a lawyer and former career diplomat who has been Prime Minister of Croatia since 19 October 2016 and president of the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) since 2016; in October 2026 he marked ten years in office, the longest tenure of any Croatian prime minister. After joining the Foreign Ministry in 1994 he worked mainly on European integration, served as deputy head of Croatia's mission to the EU and deputy ambassador in Paris, and was state secretary for European integration (2010–2011), before being elected to the Sabor in 2011 and to the European Parliament in 2013 and 2014, where he sat with the EPP group. He took over the HDZ at extraordinary party elections in 2016 and has led it to first place in the parliamentary elections of 2016, 2020 and 2024, governing first with Most, then with HNS, then with the Serb minority party SDSS and, since May 2024, with the Homeland Movement (DP). His governments handled the 2017 Agrokor crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2020 earthquakes in Zagreb and Banovina, and took Croatia into the euro area and the Schengen area on 1 January 2023; they have also seen more than thirty ministers leave office, several amid corruption investigations, according to a Dnevnik Nova TV review. As of October 2026 he leads his third cabinet, which survived the opposition's 44th attempt to bring it down on 21 October 2026 (55 votes for, 79 against), amid tensions with coalition partner DP.
